findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh logger, so logs written through it are lost
findings.body: `TestLogger.FromContext` returns `NewTestLogger()` instead of the receiver `f`. `LoggerMiddleware.logRequest` now logs via `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`, so with this fake the "Plugin Request Completed" call is recorded on a throwaway instance. The `InfoLogs`/`ErrorLogs` counters on the logger a test injected stay at zero. Any current or future test that checks the middleware's logging with this fake cannot observe the log call. Returning `f`, or a child that shares the parent's `Logs` storage, would keep the fake usable for this path.

findings.title: LoggerMiddleware now silently relies on ContextualLoggerMiddleware being earlier in the chain
findings.body: `LoggerMiddleware.logRequest` used to add `pluginId`, `endpoint`, `uname`, `dsName`, `dsUID` and `traceID` to the "Plugin Request Completed" (`grafana-data-egress`) log line itself. It now relies entirely on context attributes that `NewContextualLoggerMiddleware` sets upstream. `NewLoggerMiddleware` is exported and nothing enforces or documents this ordering. Any middleware stack built without `NewContextualLoggerMiddleware` before it (custom/enterprise stacks, tests, or a future reorder in `CreateMiddlewares`) will emit egress log lines without plugin or datasource identifiers, and nothing will fail. Consider documenting the dependency on `NewLoggerMiddleware`, or keeping a fallback that adds these fields when they are missing.

findings.title: New ContextualLoggerMiddleware and the moved log attributes have no test coverage
findings.body: This PR adds `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` and moves the plugin/datasource/user attributes out of both the old instrumentation middleware and `LoggerMiddleware`. No test checks that requests passing through the stack still carry `endpoint`, `pluginId`, `dsName`, `dsUID` and `uname` in the context. Nor does any test check that the `LoggerMiddleware` log line still includes them via `FromContext`. A regression here would drop identifying fields from production data-egress logs and no test would catch it.
